name: Hedgehog pathway agonist

lead: Hedgehog pathway agonists were explored as topical hair-growth drugs to bring dormant follicles back to producing hair.

The Hedgehog pathway is reported to be required for follicles to move from rest into the growth phase, and agonists activate it through Smoothened and GLI signalling, the opposite of anticancer Smoothened inhibitors such as vismodegib. One program is associated in community discussion with Curis and Procter & Gamble. No human efficacy results were found.

paras: No product is available, so there is no routine to follow. It is followed in hair-loss discussion as a past research direction.
According to Wikipedia, the hair-growth effort failed because of toxicities found in animal models. Activating this pathway is a concern in tissue-growth contexts in general.

angle.text: Hedgehog agonists were developed to switch on the signalling that moves follicles from rest into the growth phase, aiming at hair regrowth. The effort was reportedly discontinued over animal toxicity, and no product is available.

lead: Hedgehog pathway agonists are small molecules that switch on the Hedgehog signaling pathway, which guides embryonic development and regulates adult stem cells. The pathway is reported to be required for hair follicles to move from the resting phase into the growth phase, which is why agonists were explored as hair-growth drugs. [1]

One program is associated in community discussion with Curis and Procter & Gamble. According to Wikipedia, the hair-growth effort failed because of toxicities found in animal models. [1] No marketed product exists, and the sources reviewed describe no human efficacy data.
infobox: Development reported as failed on animal toxicity [1]

paras: In the Hedgehog pathway, the receptor Patched-1 suppresses Smoothened; when Sonic hedgehog binds Patched-1, Smoothened is released and activates GLI transcription factors. Approved drugs vismodegib (2012) and sonidegib (2015) inhibit Smoothened for basal cell carcinoma and can cause harmful side effects. [1]

Agonists work in the opposite direction. A 2005 paper titled 'Modulation of hair growth with small molecule agonists of the hedgehog signaling pathway' is cited by Wikipedia in connection with this approach. [1]

Wikipedia states that exploiting the pathway for hair growth failed due to toxicities seen in animal models, without naming the compound or sponsor. [1] The link to Curis and Procter & Gamble comes from the entry's community label and was not confirmed from the pages reviewed.

timeline.event: Paper on small-molecule Hedgehog agonists modulating hair growth published. [1]
